team|Team]]}} }} '''Destiny Usman Garuba Alari''' (born 9 March 2002) is a Spanish professional [[basketball]] player for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. Listed at {{height|m=2.03}}, he plays at both the [[power forward]] and [[center (basketball)|center]] positions. Garuba was born in [[Madrid]], Spain to Nigerian parents and joined the youth academy of Real Madrid at age 11. In 2019, when he was 17 years old, he became the youngest starter in Real Madrid history. In the 2020–21 season, Garuba was named [[EuroLeague Rising Star]] and [[ACB Best Young Player Award|ACB Best Young Player]]. He earned [[most valuable player]] (MVP) honors at the [[2016 FIBA U16 European Championship]] at age 14. In the [[2021 NBA draft]], he was selected by the [[Houston Rockets]] with the 23rd overall pick. ==Early life and youth career== Born in [[Hospital Universitario 12 de Octubre|Hospital 12 de Octubre]] in [[Madrid]], Garuba was raised in the neighborhood of Villaverde Bajo (Madrid) and the municipality of [[Azuqueca de Henares]] ([[province of Guadalajara]]).{{cite web |first=Raquel |last=Gonzalez |title=¿Quién es Usman Garuba? El madridista que manda en Europa |url=https://as.com/baloncesto/2018/08/12/mas_baloncesto/1534074312_747506.html |work=[[Diario AS]] |date=27 July 2019 |access-date=10 October 2019 |language=es}}{{cite web |first=César |last=del Río |title=Usman Garuba, la perla del Real Madrid de baloncesto que salió de la cantera del Azuqueca |url=http://www.encastillalamancha.es/deportes/usman-garuba-la-perla-del-real-madrid-baloncesto-salio-la-cantera-del-azuqueca/ |website=EnCastillaLaMancha.es |date=4 November 2017 |access-date=10 October 2019 |language=es}} He grew up playing [[association football|football]], his original passion, but switched to [[basketball]] because his exceptional height limited his success in the former sport.{{cite web |first=David |last=Hein |title=Garuba finally shines for Madrid at ANGT |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/8pcpwpgll47twfyu/garuba-finally-shines-for-madrid-at-angt |website=AdidasNGT.com |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |date=29 April 2018 |access-date=12 October 2019}} Garuba idolized former NBA player [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]]. In November 2011, he joined Escuela Municipal de Baloncesto de Azuqueca (Municipal Basketball School of Azuqueca), where coach and coordinator David Serrano helped him start his basketball career and where he earned the nickname of "La pantera de Azuqueca" ("The Panther of Azuqueca"). In 2013, Garuba joined the lower categories of [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]]. He stood {{height|m=1.89}} and weighed {{Cvt|81|kg}} by the time he was 12 years old.{{cite web |title=El "muro" gigante de 12 años del Real Madrid |url=https://www.marca.com/2014/05/28/baloncesto/basketfeb/1401261709.html |work=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |date=28 May 2014 |access-date=10 October 2019 |language=es}} In 2015, Garuba helped his team win the [[:es:Minicopa Endesa|Minicopa Endesa]], an under-14 Spanish club tournament. He debuted by posting 24 points and 16 rebounds in a win over [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]].{{cite web |title=El coloso infantil del Madrid es la sensación de la Minicopa |url=https://www.marca.com/2015/02/20/baloncesto/copa-rey/1424453935.html |work=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |date=20 February 2015 |access-date=12 October 2019 |language=es}} In the following year, Garuba led Real Madrid to another Minicopa title and was named MVP of the competition.{{cite web |title=Usman Garuba es el MVP Movistar+ de la Minicopa Endesa |url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=120501 |website=ACB.com |publisher=[[Liga ACB]] |date=21 February 2016 |access-date=12 October 2019 |language=es |archive-date=22 July 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170722223636/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=120501 |url-status=dead }} He averaged 22.8 rebounds per game in the tournament, grabbing 32 against [[Joventut Badalona]] in the final. In February 2018, Garuba gained his first [[Adidas Next Generation Tournament]] (ANGT) experience with the Real Madrid under-18 team at the [[2017–18 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament#Munich Tournament|Munich qualifying tournament]], after missing the previous edition with a quadriceps injury. He was selected to the All-Tournament Team, despite being one of the youngest participants. In the final tournament, Garuba averaged 12 points and 6.5 rebounds per game and was named ANGT Rising Star.{{cite web |title=Rytas guard Sirvydis named ANGT MVP |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/8r35meqnjihofupj/rytas-guard-sirvydis-named-angt-mvp |website=AdidasNGT.com |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |date=20 May 2018 |access-date=13 October 2019}} In January 2019, he was named MVP of the ANGT Munich tournament after averaging 16.5 points, seven rebounds and 3.8 assists per game.{{cite web |title=Garuba named MVP of ANGT Munich |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/9fc8u53ovdvnsmd7/garuba-named-mvp-of-angt-munich |website=AdidasNGT.com |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |date=27 January 2019 |access-date=13 October 2019}} Garuba helped Real Madrid win the final tournament and joined MVP [[Mario Nakić]] on the All-Tournament Team.{{cite web |first=David |last=Hein |title=MVP Nakic of U18 Real Madrid leads Munich all-tourney team |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/8j6x6vbphcwp7bln/mvp-nakic-of-u18-real-madrid-leads-munich-all-tourney-team |website=AdidasNGT.com |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |date=11 February 2018 |access-date=13 October 2019}} ==Professional career == ===Real Madrid (2017–2021)=== In the [[2017–18 Liga EBA season|2017–18 season]], Garuba played for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto B|Real Madrid B]], the [[reserve team]] for Real Madrid in the [[Liga EBA]], the [[Spanish basketball league system|fourth-tier league]] in Spain. In 11 games, he averaged 11.1 points, 9.2 rebounds and 1.7 blocks per game.{{cite web |title=Real Madrid II Statistics - Spanish League |url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/team/Spain/Real-Madrid-II/2338?Page=3&Stats=2018 |website=[[Eurobasket.com]] |access-date=13 October 2019}} In the [[2018–19 Liga EBA season|2018–19 season]], he continued to primarily play for Real Madrid B, averaging 14.6 points, 12.0 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.5 blocks per game over 22 Liga EBA appearances.{{cite web |title=Real Madrid II Statistics - Spanish League |url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/team/Spain/Real-Madrid-II/2338?Page=3&Stats=2019 |website=[[Eurobasket.com]] |access-date=13 October 2019}}{{cite web |title=La semana mágica del MVP Usman Garuba |url=http://www.feb.es/2019/2/4/baloncesto/semana-magica-del-mvp-usman-garuba/77366.aspx |website=FEB.es |publisher=[[Spanish Basketball Federation]] |date=4 February 2019 |access-date=13 October 2019 |language=es}} On 28 October 2018, at 16 years and seven months of age, Garuba debuted for Real Madrid in the [[Liga ACB]], the first-tier league in Spain, against [[CB Miraflores|Miraflores]]. He became the youngest [[center (basketball)|center]] in ACB history, surpassing [[José Ángel Antelo]], and the third-youngest Real Madrid debutant, behind [[Luka Dončić]] and [[:es:Roberto Núñez|Roberto Núñez]].{{cite web |title=Usman Garuba, el pívot más joven en debutar en la Liga Endesa |url=http://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/144180 |website=ACB.com |publisher=[[Liga ACB]] |date=28 October 2018 |access-date=13 October 2019 |language=es}} In the [[2019–20 Real Madrid Baloncesto season|2019–20 season]], Garuba became a full-time member of Real Madrid's senior team. In his season debut against [[Joventut Badalona]], at 17 years, six months and 19 days of age, he eclipsed Dončić as Real Madrid's youngest-ever starter.{{cite web |title=Garuba becomes Real Madrid's youngest-ever starter |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/09/garuba-becomes-real-madrids-youngest-ever-starter |website=RealMadrid.com |publisher=[[Real Madrid Baloncesto]] |date=28 September 2019 |access-date=13 October 2019}} On 29 September, Garuba recorded 13 points and 10 rebounds in a win over [[UCAM Murcia CB|Murcia]] to become the youngest player with a [[double (basketball)|double-double]] or 10 rebounds in ACB history; Dončić had previously held both records. He was also the second-youngest player to post an efficiency rating of 24 in the ACB, behind only [[Ricky Rubio]].{{cite web |title=Liga Endesa ¡Histórico Garuba! Supera los récords de precocidad de Doncic y Ricky Rubio |url=https://www.marca.com/baloncesto/acb/2019/09/29/5d91177846163fb4138b462d.html |work=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |date=29 September 2019 |access-date=13 October 2019 |language=es}} On 30 October 2019, Garuba made his [[EuroLeague]] debut, recording 12 points, four rebounds, three steals, and a [[Performance Index Rating]] (PIR) of 20, against [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]].{{cite web |first=Antigoni |last=Zachari |title=17-year-old Usman Garuba made his EuroLeague debut count |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/958918/17-year-old-usman-garuba-made-his-euroleague-debut-count/ |website=EuroHoops.net |date=31 October 2019 |access-date=2 November 2019}} He finished the season averaging 4.4 points, 4.4 rebounds and 0.7 blocks in 15 minutes per game in the ACB and EuroLeague and was an [[ACB Best Young Player Award|ACB All-Young Players Team]] selection.{{cite web |title=Mejor Quinteto Joven El Corte Inglés de la Liga Endesa 2019-20 |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/153499-mejor-quinteto-joven-el-corte-ingles-de-la-liga-endesa-201920.html |website=ACB.com |publisher=[[Liga ACB]] |date=25 June 2020 |access-date=27 June 2020 |language=es}}{{cite web |title=Usman Garuba Player Profile |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Usman-Garuba/Summary/108741 |url=https://www.gigantes.com/euroliga/el-real-madrid-gana-con-el-mejor-partido-euroliga-de-garuba-y-otro-recital-de-tavares/ |work=Gigantes del Basket |date=22 December 2020 |access-date=26 April 2021}} ===Houston Rockets (2021–2023)=== [[File:1_usman_garuba.jpg|thumb|Garuba with the Rockets in 2023]] In the [[2021 NBA draft]], he was drafted by the [[Houston Rockets]] with the 23rd overall He made his [[2021 NBA Summer League]] debut in a 92–76 loss versus the [[Toronto Raptors]] where he went scoreless along with six rebounds and one steal.{{cite web |title=Houston vs. Toronto - Box June 2023}} On 5 October, he made his preseason debut off the bench against the [[Washington Wizards]] in a 125–119 loss with five points and a rebound in six minutes of action.{{cite web |url=https://basketnews.com/news-248272-real-madrid-confirms-devastating-injury-news-on-usman-garuba.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=28 May 2026 |language=en}} ==National team career== ===Junior national team=== [[File:Usman Garuba (cropped).jpg|thumb|Garuba with the [[Spain national under-18 basketball team|Spain under-18 team]] in 2019]] Garuba made his junior national team debut for [[Spain men's national under-16 basketball team|Spain]] at the [[2016 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Radom]], Poland. He was named MVP after leading his team to a gold medal and averaging 16.3 points, 12.4 rebounds, and a tournament-leading 2.9 blocks per game.{{cite web |title=Usman Garuba claims MVP award to lead All-Star Five |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2016/news/usman-garuba-claims-mvp-award-to-lead-all-star-five |website=FIBA.basketball |publisher=[[FIBA]] |date=21 August 2016 |access-date=12 October 2019}} A 14-year-old and the second-youngest player in the tournament, Garuba became the first player from a lower age group to ever win MVP at the event.{{cite web |first=Mike |last=Schmitz |title=FIBA U16 European Championship Scouting Reports |url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/FIBA-U16-European-Championship-Scouting-Reports-5648/ |website=DraftExpress.com |date=22 August 2016 |access-date=13 October 2019 |archive-date=28 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220928043055/http://www.draftexpress.com/article/FIBA-U16-European-Championship-Scouting-Reports-5648/ |url-status=dead }} After recording 15 points, 11 rebounds and 10 blocks in the final against [[Lithuania men's national under-16 and under-17 basketball team|Lithuania]], he joined [[Dario Šarić]] and [[Ricky Rubio]] as the only players in history with a [[triple-double]] in the final of the tournament.{{cite web |title=Garuba happy to finally be back with his 2002 generation |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2018/news/garuba-happy-to-finally-be-back-with-his-2002-generation |website=FIBA.basketball |publisher=[[FIBA]] |date=16 August 2018 |access-date=12 October 2019}} In the summer of 2017, Garuba was unable to return to national team duty because he was recovering from a knee injury suffered earlier that year. At the [[2018 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Novi Sad]], Serbia, he averaged 16.3 points and 12.3 rebounds per game and led Spain to a silver medal, earning a spot on the All-Star Five.{{cite web |title="I told the coach to draw the last play up for me," says MVP Prkacin |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2018/news/-i-told-the-coach-to-draw-the-last-play-up-for-me-says-mvp-prkacin |website=FIBA.basketball |publisher=[[FIBA]] |date=19 August 2018 |access-date=12 October 2019}} Garuba helped Spain win a gold medal at the [[2019 FIBA U18 European Championship]] in [[Volos]], Greece, joining his teammate and MVP [[Santi Aldama]] on the All-Star Five after averaging 15.6 points, 12.9 rebounds and 2.1 blocks per game.{{cite web |title=Unstoppable Aldama headlines the All-Star Five of the FIBA U18 European Championship |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18/2019/news/unstoppable-aldama-headlines-the-all-star-five-of-the-fiba-u18-european-championship |website=FIBA.basketball |publisher=[[FIBA]] |date=4 August 2019 |access-date=13 October 2019}} ===Senior national team=== In 2021, Garuba played on [[Spain men's national basketball team]] at the [[2020 Summer Olympics]] in [[Tokyo]], Japan{{cite web |title=GARUBA Usman |url=https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/olympic-games/en/results/basketball/athlete-profile-n1400411-garuba-usman.htm |work=[[Tokyo 2020 Olympics]] |access-date=6 August 2021
